feature.name: Agent Brain — reliable agent workflow and code-aware project memory
feature.description:
Evolve Agent Plan in the same repository into a reliable, code-aware project memory and operating workflow. First address the six reported failures: orientation among phase handoffs, repeated resume context cost, ignored rules/conventions, lost return to interrupted work, inconsistent next-work priority and unnecessary task growth. Then add structured code links, task changesets, scoped decision history, capability-based multilingual setup, a queryable graph, relevant context retrieval and supervisor UI. Existing planning memory, requirements, Accepted Decisions, phase handoffs, read gates and atomic ownership already exist and must be extended rather than recreated.

Baseline: origin/main c4d0c459f74f5365c9ab8a9fe53ad6d7907a8231 on branch feat/agent-brain. Relevant completed work includes F016/F018/F020/F021/F023/F024; their historical descriptions are not proof of current behavior. Core points: packages/plan-core/src/task-selection.ts (recommendNextTask), recap.ts (buildRecap), task-context.ts (buildPhaseContextBlock), project-context.ts, read-tracking.ts, schema.ts and plan-store.ts (claimTask/Accepted Decision CRUD). Adapter surfaces: packages/plan-mcp/src/index.ts, packages/pi-adapter/src/index.ts, packages/plan-server/src/serve.ts; public projection in packages/plan-core/src/api-v1.ts and packages/plan-server/src/entity-events.ts; existing Web UI under packages/plan-web-ui/src/. Source catalog in .planner/docs/agent-brain-plan.md binds navigation lines, symbols and file hashes to the baseline; revalidate before editing.

Preserve canonical entity IDs and ownership, phase-scoped handoffs, derived parent statuses, existing human-supervisor semantics, no automatic dashboard activation and shared/local runtime boundaries. The project no-task guard decision remains warning-only; a new write-denial policy is not implicitly approved. File:line is never permanent identity. Analysis targets each user's project through an open set of compatible providers discovered/configured from extensible metadata; named languages are non-exclusive fixtures, not a planner-core whitelist. TypeScript is not a universal analyzer. Empty folders and undecided stacks are valid.

All work is planned, not implemented. The earlier 11-case TypeScript anchor proof was isolated and does not establish production or cross-language support. Standalone AgentTest, new product branding/package renames, autonomous publishing and a mandatory graph database/embedding service are outside scope. Canonical requirements, decisions, phase/task descriptions and checklists define execution; the supporting document explains contracts, sources, scenario matrix and remaining technical choices.

The complete technical handover is .planner/docs/agent-brain-registration-handoff.md, including CodeLink/CodeAnchor/AnchorResolution, the resolver and review mechanism, changeset attribution, provider setup/fallback, context retrieval and worked cases. Supporting discussion records are .planner/docs/agent-brain-discussion-scope.md and .planner/docs/agent-brain-code-links-design.md. These are design/evidence inputs; canonical entities remain authoritative.

These are registered plans, not implemented product behavior.

Approved shared-planner expansion (21 October 2026): P128(F025)/T489-T490 separates canonical plan storage, explicit code workspace and caller runtime and supplies one coordinated local authority for all supported clients. P129(F025)/T491-T493 distinguishes attributable task executions from per-target integrations and current revision-aware code availability, with separate global-work and target-delivery UI/API projections. The intended local store is outside code branch copies under git-common-dir/projectId; standalone roots remain supported, independent clones/machines require explicit transfer/service support, and exact layout/transport are implementation choices. Worktree path or branch name is not durable identity.

A verified execution in feat/due is not delivered to another target simply because dev-a merges feat/one. Historical merges remain recorded after a revert, while current availability and verification are revalidated. Targets are configurable, legacy/non-code work does not get fabricated commits/PRs, and this repository release governance is unchanged. B1 consumes availability while preserving owned work, ready returns and global priority. No implicit task done-to-shipped reinterpretation or duplicate provider is approved.

Completion of work in one branch does not assert integration into another target; legacy and non-code work preserve honest provenance and uncertainty.

requirements.title: Revision-aware target availability and delivery views
requirements.description: Agents and supervisors can distinguish global work progress from result availability in an explicitly selected checkout or configured target. Independent integration history supports multiple targets and current observations; revert/rebase/squash and uncertain equivalence cannot silently misstate readiness or delivery.

requirements.title: Lossless adoption of a shared planner from existing copies
requirements.description: A project can preview, reconcile and activate a single shared planner from divergent worktree copies without losing approved knowledge, IDs, decisions, handoffs or attributable history. Incompatible edits remain explicit and recoverable; interruption or an incompatible client cannot create a silent parallel authority.

requirements.title: Planner history and recovery independent of code commits
requirements.description: Project planning knowledge and execution/integration history remain durable without an agent committing code. Users can inspect change history, maintain independent backups and deliberately export/restore a complete portable project record including required recoverable evidence, without transferring stale live ownership or assuming Git clone/push copies it.

requirements.title: Consistent affected hierarchy and dependency context after every change
requirements.description: Agents and supervisors can trust that creating, updating or moving planner work and changing relationships checks affected task/phase/feature/project context and dependency readiness. Necessary factual updates are reconciled through their canonical owners; reviewed-unchanged and pending semantic review are explicit and revision-bound, preserving approved history and unrelated content.

requirements.title: Bounded context cost across all Agent Brain workflows
requirements.description: Routine mutation, resume, context, graph and editor workflows deliver only relevant incremental information with bounded payload/tool overhead and explicit continuation for large impact. Correctness and mandatory rules/requirements/decisions survive compaction or source/workspace changes; measured budgets and real context availability govern reuse rather than unverified token-saving claims.

decisions.title: Ready work follows global feature → phase → task priority
decisions.decision: When no owned active work or actionable pending return takes precedence, choose ready available work globally by feature priority, then phase priority, then task priority. Current-phase continuity does not override higher global priority. Dependency, block and ownership constraints remain in force.
decisions.rationale: Explicit user answer on 20 October 2026: Priorità globale feature → fase → task.
decisions.implementationNotes: Implement once in the shared core; recap, recommendations, completion, MCP/Pi/server and UI consume the same result. Respect priority zero, deterministic ties and explicit user choices.

decisions.title: Evolve Agent Plan and stabilize existing workflows first
decisions.decision: Agent Brain is an evolution in this repository. Reuse existing planner memory, requirements, decisions, tasks, checkpoints, phase handoffs and ownership. Resolve the six reported reliability problems before the code graph extensions.
decisions.rationale: The user corrected the initial gap analysis: most planning/memory structures already exist; the priority is their reliable application.
decisions.implementationNotes: Use branch feat/agent-brain from refreshed origin/main as requested. Do not create a parallel planner, forked product authority or automatic task per inventory bullet.

decisions.title: Code intelligence targets the user project and is language independent
decisions.decision: The analyzed code belongs to the project using Agent Plan. Persisted links and domain contracts are language independent. Resolve the declared or detected languages against extensible provider metadata and actual compatible tool capabilities, rather than a fixed language whitelist in planner core. TypeScript is the implementation host, not a universal source analyzer.
decisions.rationale: The user explicitly clarified on 21 October 2026 that the previously named languages are examples, not the complete supported language set.
decisions.implementationNotes: Use versioned provider manifests/catalog entries and user-configured compatible providers. Probe language/version/platform, workspace/build prerequisites and supplied operations before activation. A new language supported by an existing adapter is enabled through provider metadata/configuration, without editing planner core. A genuinely new protocol may need an adapter. Validate multiple unrelated language families and a dynamically added language fixture; Rust, C/C++, Java and JS/TS are non-exclusive examples. Keep coverage per provider, operation, configuration and source area; unsupported cases retain text/planning capabilities.

decisions.title: Code links distinguish historical evidence, current location and meaning review
decisions.decision: A file:line reference is a navigation position, not permanent identity. Preserve recoverable snapshot baselines and provenance, resolve current locations separately, and keep architectural/factual review distinct from location resolution.
decisions.rationale: The user identified stale references and explanations after code changes as dangerous.
decisions.implementationNotes: Handle dirty state and worktree/configuration identity. External rename/move/copies yield verified candidates or ambiguity; no silent semantic relinking or approved-decision rewrite.

decisions.title: Trace large work through changesets and scoped rationale
decisions.decision: Track an entire task changeset automatically and record significant decisions at the appropriate module/interface/function scope. Do not require manual documentation of every modified function. Prior tasks become discoverable through shared code targets even without task-to-task references.
decisions.rationale: The user emphasized that tasks often implement large pieces of code and unrelated tasks later modify the same function.
decisions.implementationNotes: Capture baseline/checkpoints/closeout and preserve initial dirty state. Attribute only observed task/session changes; ambiguous overlap remains explicit. Canonical decisions keep one durable owner and versioned history.

decisions.title: Provide global orientation and relevant deep context
decisions.decision: Offer a source-backed global map immediately and retrieve detailed context for the current work and its relevant impact boundaries. Do not claim that the model has instantly read or understood the entire codebase.
decisions.rationale: The user asked whether a new agent receives full codebase context or only the area of work.
decisions.implementationNotes: Retrieve applicable rules, prior rationale, correct precedents, usages/interfaces/dependencies and tests. Expose unavailable, not retrieved, stale and absent information and explicit continuation under budgets.

decisions.title: Begin setup from discussion and declared stack, not assumed source detection
decisions.decision: An empty folder with an undecided language is a valid project state. Record stack decisions during discussion and activate only needed analysis capabilities when their prerequisites are available. Later source detection validates declared choices.
decisions.rationale: The user corrected the assumption that discussion always starts in an existing repository.
decisions.implementationNotes: Use an extensible versioned provider catalog and explicit configured-provider entries, not a closed language enum. Resolve matching providers, reuse compatible local tools or produce a concrete preparation/configuration plan under existing installation policy, then validate real results. Protocols do not provide universal server/indexer discovery or installation. SCIP ingestion, live LSP and syntax parsing are complementary options, not three mandatory universal installations. Keep managed tools outside user application dependencies and preserve stack-undecided projects.

decisions.title: Extend existing standards workflow with evidence rather than repeated instructions
decisions.decision: Read and apply existing project rules and appropriate implementation precedents before writing code; preserve evidence and review final conformity. Extend the existing canonical skill/protocol instead of presenting these obligations as new functionality.
decisions.rationale: Explicit user report: agents already receive these instructions but ignore established code conventions.
decisions.implementationNotes: Preserve project decision 7995854e-4109-48aa-b08b-a54bff4d8432 on the warning-only no-task guard. New write-denial policy is not implicitly approved. Observed reads and a checked checklist do not prove semantic conformity; document actual harness coverage and qualitative review.

decisions.title: Keep skills portable and canonical knowledge authoritative
decisions.decision: Use the existing core/shared skill distribution for all supported harnesses. Adapt useful external skill/rule/hook patterns without making Claude-specific configuration or a derived graph the authority over the planner.
decisions.rationale: The user requested generalized Agent Plan skills inspired by Everything Claude Code, usable by all agents.
decisions.implementationNotes: Domain policies stay in core. Preserve canonical versus local runtime boundaries; graph/index packets are derived. Existing single-owner decisions and phase-scoped handoffs remain authoritative.

decisions.title: Keep standalone AgentTest outside this feature
decisions.decision: Use and link existing tests and revision-bound verification evidence for Agent Brain. A separate autonomous test generation/execution product called AgentTest is not a prerequisite or an implicitly included development stream.
decisions.rationale: AgentTest was an earlier concept, not an identified existing repository; the agreed scope prioritized the six failures and code graph.
decisions.implementationNotes: Leave an explicit extension seam for test evidence and future integrations, and document missing coverage. Do not add a separate planner or AI testing platform under this feature.

decisions.title: Use Monaco for the desktop source-code workspace
decisions.decision: Use Monaco Editor for the integrated file explorer, editable source tabs, syntax coloring and diff. Source editing/saving is included. Mobile code editing is not a deciding acceptance requirement; preserve existing planner responsiveness and document actual limitations.
decisions.rationale: The user selected an experience like the adjacent file explorer and clarified that mobile source editing is not a meaningful reason to prefer CodeMirror. Monaco is the resulting choice.
decisions.implementationNotes: Load Monaco/workers/language assets on demand and ship them locally; retain the lightweight existing Markdown workflow. Choose a compatible tested integration stack and versions without assuming VS Code extension compatibility. Do not install dependencies or implement product code as part of this planning update.

decisions.title: Share analysis through one compatible runtime owner
decisions.decision: Agents and the editor use the same analysis service. Reuse one compatible language-server runtime for the same project/worktree, provider/version and effective configuration; the frontend does not start a duplicate process by default.
decisions.rationale: The user asked whether Agent Plan and the embedded editor would run two LSP servers. The agreed architecture explicitly avoids duplication merely because both consumers exist.
decisions.implementationNotes: Extend P121 contracts with broker-owned upstream sessions, atomic cross-host-process ownership/reuse, cancellation, consumer lifecycle and named document revisions/overlays. Monaco provider hooks call common APIs; an optional frontend LSP client/gateway must not independently initialize a competing server. Separate keys may require separate runtimes, and provider capabilities remain dynamic.

decisions.title: Put project identity first in browser page titles
decisions.decision: The actual project name must identify the overview and prefix entity-detail browser titles. Task detail follows ProjectName - TaskID [Short task title]; feature and phase details follow the same project-first convention.
decisions.rationale: The user cannot distinguish projects when tabs show only Agent Plan or a task title. Both reported title failures must be corrected.
decisions.implementationNotes: Use one route-aware title owner, preserve known project context through navigation/live renames/errors, retain full variable-width refs and avoid stale cleanup restoration. The bracketed description means the short entity title, not the full Markdown task description.

decisions.title: One shared planner authority outside code branch copies
decisions.decision: Local worktrees of one project use one canonical planner authority discovered through project identity and git-common-dir, with explicit standalone roots for non-Git projects. Live global planner state is not transported by ordinary code PRs.
decisions.rationale: Sharing branch copies or merging all live progress through dev-a code can report dev-b work as delivered without its code. Independent local copies also lose coordination and conflict.
decisions.implementationNotes: Use M1/M2 and O1/O2. The intended default is <git-common-dir>/agent-plan/<projectId>/; exact layout/transport is an implementation choice. Keep open JSON formats and an explicit cross-clone/service boundary; no implicit cloud or distributed consistency.

decisions.title: Planner, code workspace and caller runtime have separate identities
decisions.decision: planRoot, workspaceRoot and runtimeRoot are resolved independently. Canonical knowledge and task claims are shared, while focus, returns, context attestations, source/provider caches and overlays are scoped by their actual caller/workspace/revision owners.
decisions.rationale: Current code derives source/runtime paths from planner location. Blind centralization would mix worktrees or make agents read the central directory as source.
decisions.implementationNotes: M1/M2 own binding and coordination. Preserve stable workspace identity through path/branch changes, atomic claims and explicit recovery. K2 reuses this boundary but continues to own the single compatible language-server runtime; UI view changes cannot redirect active executions.

decisions.title: A logical task has executions and independent target integrations
decisions.decision: Keep one logical task with attributable execution attempts and exact-revision evidence; represent integration of produced results into each configured target separately. A verified execution does not mean code is present in the target.
decisions.rationale: An agent can finish in a worktree while another agent merges unrelated code. A path/branch flag or single done state cannot represent that safely.
decisions.implementationNotes: N1/N2/N3 own the model/projections, E2 owns changeset capture. Preserve phase-scoped handoffs, dirty snapshot evidence and unknown legacy provenance. Non-code tasks do not require fabricated commits/PRs. Targets are configurable; develop/next/main release governance is unchanged.

decisions.title: Current code availability differs from work progress and historical merges
decisions.decision: Expose global operational progress separately from workspace/target availability and delivery. Revalidate source-dependent evidence at the selected revision; use artifact availability only for tasks that need that code, preserving global priority within ready work.
decisions.rationale: A historical PR merge may be followed by a revert or changed implementation, and squash/rebase can change SHA identity without removing the result.
decisions.implementationNotes: N2 supplies bounded integration observations; N3 supplies availability and separate UI/API counters; B1 remains selector owner. Distinguish present/absent/unknown/review-required and invalidate stale evidence rather than promising general semantic equivalence.

decisions.title: Shared-planner adoption requires lossless migration and independent recovery
decisions.decision: Inventory and back up every old planner copy, reconcile with provenance and explicit conflicts, then activate one recoverable binding. Maintain durable history/checkpoints, independent backup and portable export/restore because central files are not cloned/pushed automatically.
decisions.rationale: Moving out of branch copies removes implicit Git distribution and exposes data loss if a clone is deleted or migration discards divergent knowledge.
decisions.implementationNotes: O1/O2 own migration and durability; I1/I2 own full cross-surface and installed closeout. No mtime-wins, silent fallback, invented provenance or automatic Git/tracking change. This approval registers the work only; it does not execute the migration.

decisions.title: Every mutation reconciles affected context through bounded deltas
decisions.decision: Task/phase/feature/project mutations and relationship changes must assess and reconcile affected ancestors and dependencies. Update only genuinely changed facts; record version-bound reviewed-unchanged or durable pending obligations. Apply a measured incremental-context budget to every F025 workflow.
decisions.rationale: The user requires parent/dependency consistency without excessive token consumption. Existing instructions and timestamps alone do not ensure semantic consistency or efficient context.
decisions.implementationNotes: M3 (P128(F025)/T496) owns the shared impact/postcondition protocol; C2/D2/G3/B1 consume it and I1/I2 verify it. Use maintained impact indexes, expected revisions, compact receipts, effective-context-aware reuse and paginated continuation. Do not blindly rewrite ancestors, auto-revise decisions, invent edges or drop mandatory context. No new source-write denial policy or arbitrary fixed token-saving percentage is approved.

guidelinesAppend:
## Agent Brain implementation workflow

Before modifying code for this feature, read the applicable project instructions, canonical Guidelines and Accepted Decisions, the exact feature/phase/task, and relevant existing implementations, interfaces and tests. Record a concise source-backed analysis on the existing task: precedents and their relevance, conventions, reuse, architectural ownership, intended integration and verification. Explicit rules and approved decisions take precedence over incompatible legacy examples. If no relevant precedent exists, state that fact and resolve material missing conventions through the existing discussion process.

Apply the existing lifecycle and ownership rules; preserve phase-scoped handoffs, canonical IDs and dependency edges. Use checklists for implementation details instead of creating more tasks. Before completing work, compare the actual diff with the selected precedents and applicable rules and record concrete verification and conformity evidence, including what remains unverified. A read receipt, ticked checklist or passing build alone is not architectural proof.

Reuse valid available context and refresh affected evidence after context loss, source changes or an expansion into another area. Follow existing authorization; do not add a permission prompt for every routine already authorized step. Preserve the accepted warning-only no-task guard. Never modify AGENTS.md, publish, release, push or open a PR without the authorization those actions require.

Keep source code and technical product text in English and preserve the existing React/component/test conventions. Follow the bounded verification and tracked web-ui-dist rules in AGENTS.md. Supporting Agent Brain design is under .planner/docs/agent-brain-plan.md; canonical planner entities and decisions remain the operational authority.

scenarios: Several phase handoffs after a long absence
Purpose/state/blockers are understandable and recommendation agrees with current canonical state.
A → B → C detours with temporary phase completion
Unwind C → B → A; preserve unavailable returns and session recovery.
Global priority versus current phase
Higher global ready work wins; active work, returns, ownership and dependencies remain authoritative.
Compaction, restart, same session with lost context
Restore actual required content; do not trust timestamp-only memory.
Concurrent callers and ownership recovery
No foreign-owner success, duplicate claims or recovery of a live caller.
Duplicate capability and task proliferation
Reuse open/completed ownership, current checklist or ideas inbox as appropriate.
Reference shift/refactor/copy/delete/parse failure
Resolve or explicitly expose candidates/ambiguity/unknown; preserve history and reject stale/foreign indexes.
Unsupported language or missing provider configuration
Keep planner/text use available; do not report unknown usages as zero.
Empty folder with undecided then agreed stack
Discussion works before language detection; prerequisites control actual analysis readiness.
T002 → T010 → T020 across unrelated phases
Recover current signature, prior parameter purpose and durable slim/functional constraints.
Large task with dirty baseline and overlapping work
Trace the changeset/module outcome without false attribution or per-function manual notes.
New component that compiles but violates local architecture
Use the correct precedents; detect/report missing analysis and reject nonconforming completion in review.
Dynamic provider registration and polyglot fixtures

Enable an additional language through metadata/configuration on an existing adapter; verify real providers from unrelated families, configuration and per-operation coverage, with explicit FFI/JNI/dynamic/external limits.
Requirements and graph API/event compatibility
Requirement links remain discoverable, projections preserve IDs and clients remain compatible.
Supervisor graph/review/setup workflows
Show actionable provenance, coverage and freshness while preserving hierarchy and role boundaries.
Freshly packed installed artifacts and real harness entry points
Verify actual supported runtime paths and exact fingerprints, with bounded logs and no release side effects.
Variable-width feature, phase and task references

Exercise 999→1000, 9999→10000 and larger valid values on isolated fixtures: allocation, composite/bare refs, numeric ordering/search, dependencies, parked returns, API/MCP/Pi, export and Web UI; preserve identity and reject partial or incorrect-parent matches.
Project identity across browser navigation
Overview and all detail routes retain the known project name; task format is ProjectName - TaskID [Short task title], including live renames, back/forward and known-context error/loading.
Editable Monaco workspace with concurrent writes
Open files/tabs, edit and compare; stale saves preserve draft/current content and source changes invalidate affected evidence.
Shared analysis and explicit document versions
Simultaneous supported agent/editor consumers reuse one compatible provider process, including startup races, disconnect/restart and explicit saved/draft snapshots.
Preferred editor and target-machine semantics
A resolved file opens through local configured launchers with literal paths and supported positions; remote machines and unsaved drafts remain explicit.
Shared authority with isolated callers/workspaces
Two worktrees and supported hosts share canonical knowledge and atomic claims without mixing source roots, returns, read receipts or caches.
dev-a integrated while dev-b verified elsewhere
Global progress retains both executions; the target contains only demonstrated available code and code-dependent successors receive honest readiness.
Integration history and current revision availability
Multi-target ordinary/squash/rebase/cherry-pick observations remain historical after revert; current availability/verification invalidate or become unknown.
Divergent planner migration and interrupted activation
Full backups and ID-based reconciliation preserve every decision/handoff; incompatible edits and partial activation remain explicit/recoverable.
Independent history backup and complete restore
Restore canonical entities, executions/integrations and recoverable evidence without stale live ownership or requiring a code commit.
Standalone roots and clone/worktree identity changes
Empty/non-Git binding works, moved/deleted worktrees preserve history, and new clones require deliberate transfer/rebinding.
Every mutation checks hierarchy and dependency impact
Task creation/update/move and edge/priority/scope changes reconcile affected parents through project and actual consumers, with version-bound unchanged or explicit pending assessments.
Bounded payload and effective context across all flows

Comparable mutation/resume/graph/editor fixtures measure bytes/chars/tool calls and honest token metrics; local deltas ignore unrelated growth, fan-out paginates and mandatory context survives compaction.
